d.why: Capt. 'Raygun' MacLai is one of the F-16 pilots who radio orders to the X-Jet and fire on it in a single chase scene; she has no part of her own and the scene changes nothing for her.
Wilkins is one of Stryker's soldiers at Alkali Lake with no lines or actions of his own that the story turns on.
Smith is one of Stryker's soldiers with no lines or actions of his own that the story turns on.
Abrahams, the President's chief of staff, is only present at the White House scenes and does nothing that moves the story.
B. Singer is director Bryan Singer's walk-on as a guard at Magneto's plastic prison, with no lines and no part in the story.
Sean is a museum security guard seen in one brief scene that changes nothing.

President McKenna is the target of Nightcrawler's brainwashed attack, authorises Stryker's raid on the Xavier school, and is confronted by Xavier and the X-Men in the Oval Office at the end, with lines throughout.
Flick is one of Danica Talos's vampire crew with no lines or actions of his own that the story turns on.
Wolfe is a House of Talos vampire with one line on the expedition to Dracula's tomb, a find that belongs to Danica's group; he has no part of his own.
Campbell is one of the House of Talos vampires with no lines or actions of his own that the story turns on.
Bentley Tittle hosts the TV talk show where Dr. Vance and Chief Vreede attack Blade; he only asks questions and laughs in that one segment, which changes nothing he does.
Gedge is one of Danica Talos's vampire crew with no lines or actions of his own that the story turns on.
Virago is one of Danica Talos's vampire crew with no lines or actions of her own that the story turns on.
Dingo is one of Danica Talos's vampire crew with no lines or actions of his own that the story turns on.
Nick Manolis is the NYPD captain who leads the police at the church, orders his men to fire on Daredevil and Bullseye, and arrests the wounded Bullseye.
Stavros is a Natchios bodyguard who only walks Nikolas to his car in one brief scene that changes nothing.
Stan Lee appears as himself in a wordless walk-on as the old man young Matt stops at a crossing, with no story role.
Elektra's mother appears only in Elektra's flashbacks and is spoken of ('my mother died when I was young'), with no lines of her own.
Jimmy O'Hoolihan is the Baxter Building doorman who speaks in both Fantastic Four and Rise of the Silver Surfer, including asking Doom if he is okay.
Ben Mulroney is a real TV reporter appearing as himself in the Fantastic Four news coverage.
Taryn Winter Brill is a real TV presenter appearing as herself in Fantastic Four.
Sara Edwards is a real TV host appearing as herself in Fantastic Four.
Liam Mayclem is a real entertainment reporter appearing as himself in Fantastic Four.
Shaheem Reid is a real music journalist appearing as himself in Fantastic Four.
Sam Rubin is a real entertainment anchor appearing as himself in Fantastic Four.
Maria Salas is a real reporter appearing as herself in Fantastic Four.
Devon Soltendieck is a real presenter appearing as himself in the Fantastic Four news coverage.
Patrick Stoner is a real film reporter appearing as himself in Fantastic Four.
